description:
Saves the mail settings; send only what changes. Fields set by environment variables are ignored. An empty or omitted password keeps the saved one, password_clear removes it. A changed host, port, security or username is checked first: the host must resolve and must not be an address outbound requests may not reach (400 otherwise), and security none with a login is only allowed to a private network address. The settings decide where mail and its login go, so a session is required.

Needs: a signed-in session (API tokens are refused). Administrators only

host.description: The mail server (SMTP host name or IP address); empty when not set

security.description: How the connection is secured: starttls, tls (implicit TLS) or none. Default: starttls

verify_tls.description: Whether the server's certificate must be valid. Default: on

username.description: The login name; empty sends no login

from_address.description: The sender address of every mail; empty when not set

from_name.description: The sender name shown with the address; may be empty

reply_to.description: The address replies go to; may be empty

allow_password_reset.description: Whether users may reset a forgotten password by mail. Turning it on needs the public URL

password.description: The password, empty keeps the saved one

password_clear.description: Remove the saved password (ignored when password is sent)

200.description: The mail settings as they are now
